item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Communications
Centre for Development of Telematics excels in Intellectual Property creation with expanding portfolio of Patents and Awardees
C-DOT hosts annual IP Awards ceremony 2026 to honour 64 Scientists to recognise innovation and excellence achieved by C-DOT Delhi Campus
47 Patents, 3 Copyrights, and 8 Research papers achieved by C-DOT Delhi Campus acknowledged during IPR day function at C-DOT Delhi
Posted On: 31 JUL 2026 7:43PM by PIB Delhi

The Centre for Development of Telematics (C-DOT), the premier telecom R&D centre of the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications, Government of India, successfully organised the Annual IP Awards Ceremony 2026 to recognise and celebrate outstanding contributions from its Delhi campus in the field of Intellectual Property (IP).

The ceremony honoured C-DOT researchers and innovators whose pioneering work continues to strengthen India's indigenous telecom technology ecosystem and advance the nation's vision of technology-led growth.

A total of 47 patents, 3 copyrights, and 8 research papers were recognised, with awards conferred upon 64 individuals for their innovation and excellence at C-DOT Delhi. The event recognised the outstanding contributions of researchers, engineers, and domain experts whose pioneering work has significantly strengthened C-DOT's intellectual property portfolio. With a steadily expanding patent portfolio and a growing number of innovators being recognised for their excellence, C-DOT continues to reinforce its position as a premier telecom R&D institution driving indigenous technological innovation. These accomplishments underscore the organisation's sustained commitment to research excellence, intellectual property creation, and the development of globally competitive technologies that contribute to India's vision of technological self-reliance and digital transformation.

Congratulating the awardees, Dr. Rajkumar Upadhyay, CEO, C-DOT, said, “Innovation is the cornerstone of C-DOT's mission to build indigenous, secure and future-ready telecom technologies for the nation. Every patent, publication and intellectual asset created by our researchers strengthens India's technological sovereignty and reinforces our commitment to the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat. These awards recognise not only exceptional technical excellence but also the spirit of curiosity, perseverance and innovation that drives C-DOT's research ecosystem. I congratulate all the awardees and encourage them to continue developing transformative technologies that contribute to India's emergence as a global telecom innovation leader."

Over the years, C-DOT has built a robust intellectual property portfolio spanning next-generation communication technologies, cybersecurity, quantum communications, disaster management systems, AI-driven telecom solutions and digital public infrastructure. C-DOT remains committed to translating research excellence into impactful technologies that address national priorities while enhancing India's competitiveness in the global telecommunications landscape.

Recently, C-DOT also organised the Annual IP Awards Ceremony 2026 at its Bengaluru campus, where 78 innovators were honoured for their exceptional contributions to Intellectual Property creation. The ceremony recognised 36 patents, 18 copyrights, 9 trademarks, and 3 research papers, reflecting the depth and diversity of innovation across the organisation. Together, the IP Awards ceremonies at the Delhi and Bengaluru campuses highlight C-DOT's continued commitment on innovation, intellectual property creation, and the development of indigenous technologies that contribute to India's growing leadership in the telecommunications sector.

item.category: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
item.description: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways Cabinet Approved Revised Policy for Award of Waterfront and Associated Land to Port Dependent Industries (PDI) in Major Ports Revised Policy allows existing captive users to add new berth/jetty/terminal/single buoy mooring (SBM) for Enhanced Captive Requirement upto 30 years for Government entities Competitive bidding with RoFR to unlock fresh capacity expansion at major ports Government entities gain Direct Access to Waterfront under new policy Posted On: 31 JUL 2026 7:38PM by PIB Delhi NEW DELHI, July 31, 2026: The Union…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
Cabinet Approved Revised Policy for Award of Waterfront and Associated Land to Port Dependent Industries (PDI) in Major Ports
Revised Policy allows existing captive users to add new berth/jetty/terminal/single buoy mooring (SBM) for Enhanced Captive Requirement upto 30 years for Government entities
Competitive bidding with RoFR to unlock fresh capacity expansion at major ports
Government entities gain Direct Access to Waterfront under new policy
Posted On: 31 JUL 2026 7:38PM by PIB Delhi

NEW DELHI, July 31, 2026: The Union Cabinet has approved a revised Policy for Award of Waterfront and Associated Land to Port Dependent Industries (Captive Policy), introducing a series of reforms aimed at accelerating private investment through the Public Private Partnership (PPP) model, improving operational flexibility and strengthening infrastructure development across India's major ports.

The revised policy updates the existing Captive Policy of 2016 by enabling existing captive users to expand capacity through new berths, jetties, terminals and single buoy moorings (SBMs), while also providing a framework for extending concession agreements, awarding waterfront to eligible government entities and addressing changes arising from evolving business and regulatory conditions.

Union Minister for Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW) Sarbananda Sonowal said the revised policy reflects the government's commitment to creating a predictable, transparent and investor-friendly framework for port-led industrial growth.

"The revised Captive Policy is a major reform that balances investor confidence with public interest. By providing long-term certainty to existing operators, facilitating capacity expansion and creating a transparent framework for future investments, we are strengthening India's maritime infrastructure to support the country's rise as a global trade and logistics hub under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi," Sonowal said.

The policy is expected to provide greater certainty to investors, facilitate capacity augmentation and improve ease of doing business in the port sector without any financial implication for the Government.

One of the key reforms allows Major Port Authorities to renew or extend concession agreements of existing Port Dependent Industries (PDIs) for up to 30 years without requiring a fresh tender process. The renewal will be undertaken at either the prevailing market rate or the indexed revenue payable under the existing concession agreement, whichever is higher, protecting port revenues while providing long-term certainty to investors.

The policy also creates a structured mechanism for capacity expansion by existing captive users. Major Port Authorities will undertake price discovery through competitive bidding, while providing the existing concessionaire a Right of First Refusal (RoFR) to match the highest bid. Participation will be restricted to eligible Port Dependent Industries handling the same cargo profile, ensuring competitive price discovery while maintaining operational continuity. To prevent misuse of the expansion route for extending concession tenure, the concession period for any additional berth or terminal developed under the expansion proposal will remain co-terminus with the maximum permissible concession period of the existing facility.

Waterfront Access for Government Bodies

For the first time, the policy provides a framework for awarding waterfront and associated land to eligible government organisations without resorting to competitive bidding, subject to availability and prescribed safeguards. Eligible entities include Central and State Government departments, statutory authorities, autonomous bodies, Central and State Public Sector Undertakings (CPSUs and SPSUs), and government-controlled joint ventures operating in sectors such as fertilizers, food, petroleum, oil and gas, coal, steel and other sectors notified by the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways.The concessions will be awarded at the notified floor price.

Recognising the evolving nature of global trade, the revised policy introduces provisions for Change in Law and Unforeseen Events, allowing business plans and cargo profiles to be revised where regulatory changes or unforeseen circumstances affect project viability.

"The maritime sector operates in a dynamic global environment. This policy provides the flexibility needed to adapt to changing realities while ensuring continuity of investment, trade and port operations," said Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal.

The revised policy addresses key gaps in the 2016 framework by providing long-term certainty for investors, enabling capacity expansion in line with industrial demand and introducing greater operational flexibility for captive facilities. It also permits changes in cargo profile after the prescribed lock-in period, or immediately where necessitated by a change in law, ensuring business continuity in a dynamic global trading environment.

The Government expects the reforms to catalyse fresh investment in port infrastructure, strengthen supply chains, reduce logistics risks for port-dependent industries and generate employment through expansion of port-led industrial activity. The policy will be implemented across all Major Ports and is expected to increase cargo throughput, improve utilisation of waterfront assets and generate sustained revenue for ports without any financial implication for the Government of India.

The policy will be implemented across all Major Ports for captive facilities and is expected to improve cargo throughput, optimise utilisation of waterfront assets and generate sustained revenue for ports without any financial implication for the Government of India.

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi received a telephone call today from the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, H.E. Andy Burnham.

Prime Minister Modi warmly congratulated Prime Minister Burnham on assuming office and conveyed his best wishes for a successful tenure.

The two leaders discussed ways to further strengthen the India-UK Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. They agreed to deepen cooperation across priority areas including technology, innovation, defence, security, clean energy, education and people-to-people ties, in line with the India-UK Vision 2035.

The leaders also welcomed the recent entry into force of the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement and reaffirmed their commitment to fully harness its trade and investment potential for the shared prosperity and well-being of the people of both countries.

They also exchanged views on regional and global issues of mutual interest.

The two leaders agreed to remain in touch.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
CAQM issues Amendment to Direction No. 98 extending timeline for implementation of Revised PM emission Standards for Industries across Delhi-NCR
Posted On: 31 JUL 2026 7:26PM by PIB Delhi

The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) issued an Amendment to its Statutory Direction No. 98 regarding implementation of the revised Particulate Matter (PM) emission standards for industries operating across Delhi-NCR. The revised PM emission standard would now come into effect from 01.10.2026. The amendment was issued after consideration of the recommendations of the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) and representations received from industries and industrial associations in relation to the prevailing status of compliance with the revised emission norms.

The Direction No. 98, notified on 20.02.2026, had prescribed a uniform and stringent PM emission standard of 50 mg/Nm³ for identified categories of industries across Delhi-NCR, based on technical recommendations of CPCB and studies undertaken by IIT Kanpur. The Commission reiterated that the revised PM emission standard continues to remain technically achievable and environmentally necessary for reducing industrial emissions and improving ambient air quality in the region.

Subsequent to issuance of the Direction, CPCB, in coordination with the NCR State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs) and the Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC), undertook extensive efforts to facilitate compliance, including issuance of Directions to the concerned agencies, development of a dedicated online portal for monitoring installation and retrofitting of Air Pollution Control Devices (APCDs) and periodic review of the implementation status. During this process, industry associations highlighted certain practical challenges in meeting the prescribed timelines, including extended procurement and installation periods for APCDs, limited availability of agencies for adequacy assessment and capacity constraints of recognized laboratories for compliance verification. CPCB accordingly recommended extension of the compliance timelines as stipulated in Direction No. 98.

After examining all relevant submissions, the CAQM concluded that a limited extension of the implementation timeline would facilitate effective and uniform compliance by industries without compromising the objective of reducing industrial emissions. Accordingly, through the Amendment to Direction No. 98, the Commission revised the implementation schedule and stipulated that the revised PM emission standard of 50 mg/Nm³ would now become applicable to all industries covered under Clause 21(i) of Direction No. 98 with effect from 01.10.2026. All other provisions, stipulations and conditions contained in Direction No. 98 dated 20th February 2026 would remain unchanged.

The amendment is intended solely to provide additional time for industries to complete the necessary installation, retrofitting and assessment of APCDs, while ensuring full compliance with the stringent particulate matter emission standards within the revised timeline.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
GeM Launches 10-Day Celebrations Ahead of 10th Foundation Day, Unveils Commemorative Logo
GeM Honour Buyers, Sellers and Employees For Their Contribution Towards Success of GeM
Posted On: 31 JUL 2026 6:38PM by PIB Delhi

Government e Marketplace (GeM) today formally launched the 10-day celebrations leading up to its 10th Foundation Day, marking the beginning of a series of stakeholder engagement initiatives commemorating a decade of transforming public procurement through technology, transparency and inclusivity.

The celebrations commenced with the unveiling of the official GeM 10th Foundation Day logo, symbolising ten years of GeM's journey in building India's trusted digital public procurement ecosystem. A concept film on the commemorative logo was also screened, showcasing GeM's evolution, key milestones and vision for the future.

Addressing the gathering, CEO, GeM, Mihir Kumar, reflected on the organisation's transformative journey over the past decade and outlined its vision for the next phase of growth, innovation and stakeholder-centric public procurement.

The event also witnessed the launch of the latest edition of GeM Bharti, the organisation's in-house Hindi magazine, and recognised employees for their exemplary contributions and long service.

As part of the celebrations, GeM will organise a Buyer Meet on 5 August and a Seller Roundtable on 10 August, culminating in the 10th Foundation Day celebrations. The occasion will also honour distinguished buyers and sellers for their exemplary contributions to strengthening the GeM ecosystem.

The launch of the Foundation Day celebrations also marks the beginning of a year-long series of stakeholder engagement initiatives and outreach programmes across the country. Through special events, dialogues and collaborative platforms, GeM will bring together buyers, sellers, policymakers, industry representatives and ecosystem partners to celebrate a decade of transforming public procurement while showcasing its contribution to promoting transparent, efficient and inclusive governance across India.

item.title: Government Strengthens Safety and Dignity of Sanitation Workers Through Mechanisation and Rehabilitation Initiatives
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
item.description: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Government Strengthens Safety and Dignity of Sanitation Workers Through Mechanisation and Rehabilitation Initiatives Over 2.71 Lakh PPE Kits Distributed Under NAMASTE Scheme; More Than 1.81 Lakh Sanitation Workers Covered Under Health Insurance Posted On: 31 JUL 2026 6:31PM by PIB Delhi The Central Government has reaffirmed its commitment to ensuring the safety, dignity and socio-economic rehabilitation of sanitation workers through sustained efforts to eliminate hazardous manual cleaning practices and promote mechanised…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Government Strengthens Safety and Dignity of Sanitation Workers Through Mechanisation and Rehabilitation Initiatives
Over 2.71 Lakh PPE Kits Distributed Under NAMASTE Scheme; More Than 1.81 Lakh Sanitation Workers Covered Under Health Insurance
Posted On: 31 JUL 2026 6:31PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Government has reaffirmed its commitment to ensuring the safety, dignity and socio-economic rehabilitation of sanitation workers through sustained efforts to eliminate hazardous manual cleaning practices and promote mechanised sanitation across the country. Through the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) Scheme and rehabilitation measures for identified manual scavengers, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to strengthen occupational safety, livelihood opportunities and social protection for sanitation workers while advancing the objective of safe and dignified sanitation services.

This information was given by the Hon'ble Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, Ramdas Athawale, in a written reply to Shri Mallikarjun Kharge.

The Government informed that the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE), launched in 2023, is focused on replacing hazardous manual cleaning practices with mechanised solutions while ensuring the safety and well-being of sewer and septic tank workers and waste pickers. Since the launch of the scheme, 2,71,155 Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) kits have been distributed to sanitation workers and waste pickers. Simultaneously, 1,023 sanitation workers have received capital assistance for procuring mechanised cleaning equipment, 20,293 beneficiaries have undergone occupational safety and skill development training, and 1,81,062 beneficiaries have been covered under health insurance, significantly strengthening occupational safety and social security for sanitation workers.

The Government further informed that, according to the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis, 332 sanitation workers lost their lives while undertaking hazardous sewer and septic tank cleaning between 1 January 2021 and 30 June 2026. During this period, full compensation has been paid in 268 cases, while partial compensation has been provided in 18 cases. The Government also stated that no reports of injuries to sanitation and waste management workers have been received from the States and Union Territories.

The reply also highlighted the Government's continued efforts towards the rehabilitation of identified manual scavengers. Surveys conducted in 2013 and 2018 identified 58,098 manual scavengers across the country. Rehabilitation support has been extended through one-time cash assistance, skill development and financial assistance for self-employment. All identified beneficiaries have received one-time cash assistance, while 27,926 beneficiaries have undergone skill development training and 2,803 beneficiaries have received capital subsidy for establishing general self-employment projects, enabling sustainable livelihood opportunities.

The Central Government reiterated that it remains committed to ensuring that sanitation workers are able to work in safe, dignified and mechanised environments while receiving comprehensive social protection, skill development and livelihood support. Through sustained investments under the NAMASTE Scheme and rehabilitation initiatives, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to work towards eliminating hazardous manual cleaning practices and improving the quality of life of sanitation workers and their families across the country.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Communications
TRAI Hosts Workshop to Improve Quality of Audit in Digital Addressable Systems ( DAS ) Ecosystem
Posted On: 31 JUL 2026 6:07PM by PIB Delhi

The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) today organised a workshop for the training of empanelled audit firms for Digital Addressable Systems (DAS) audit. Hosted at TRAI Headquarters in New Delhi, the workshop underscores a major step toward promoting regulatory compliance and fostering greater transparency across the television broadcasting distribution ecosystem.

Attended by TRAI-empanelled auditors and representatives from the broadcasting industry i.e. broadcasters as well as Distribution Platform Operators, the day-long workshop served as a valuable platform for exchanging observations, insights, learnings, and experiences gained during audit processes. The workshop was attended by 81 participants in physical mode and 52 participants through online mode.

To address the issues related to audit framework, amendments to the Interconnection Regulation and audit Manual have been issued this year which are effective from 1st April 2026. The salient features of the amended regulation include:

 

  • Clearly defined timelines for audits; wherein distributors have to conduct audit and submit audit report to broadcasters by 30th September every year.

 

  • Audit is to be done on financial year basis in place of earlier calendar year.

 

  • Broadcasters can depute their representative during audit to ensure transparency and credibility of the audit process.

 

  • If broadcasters find inadequacies/discrepancies in audit report, they can seek clarifications from the auditor through DPO. Auditors must address the same in a time-bound manner.

 

  • If broadcaster is not satisfied with these clarifications, it can get the audit conducted at its own cost, after obtaining approval of the Authority.

 

  • In case a broadcaster does not receive the audit report by 30th September from the distributor, it can cause audit of such a distributor.

 

  • To promote ease of doing business, the requirement of annual audit at DPOs cost has been made optional for distributors with fewer than 30000 subscribers. However, broadcasters can get such DPOs audited at broadcasters’ cost.

 

Quote from TRAI Chairman

“TRAI’s primary objective is to foster a fair and equitable environment for all stakeholders. Its regulatory decisions reflect a commitment to balancing the interests of broadcasters, distributors, and other service providers, while placing consumer welfare at the heart of the decision-making process,” said Shri Anil Kumar Lahoti, Chairman, TRAI.

He added, “Audits conducted by TRAI-empanelled auditors are essential to ensure that the systems deployed by Distribution Platform Operators (DPOs) conform to the prescribed technical requirements. The annual audit process verifies the accuracy of both technical and commercial reports, including subscriber declarations and compliance with addressable system requirements relating to Conditional Access Systems (CAS), Subscriber Management Systems (SMS), fingerprinting, and other regulatory provisions. By ensuring transparency, accountability, and adherence to established standards, these audits play a vital role in strengthening and sustaining a trust-based broadcasting ecosystem.”

The workshop was convened following industry requests made to the Authority for periodic training of auditors on audit processes and procedures, and for improving the quality of audit reports by aligning audit outcomes with technical and commercial requirements. Sessions featured expert presentations by BECIL, audit firms, and industry stakeholders.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Jal Shakti
Jan Bhagidari Powers Groundwater Revival in Vizianagaram under Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari: Catch the Rain
Posted On: 31 JUL 2026 5:57PM by PIB Delhi

Inspired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's appeal in the 135th edition of Mann Ki Baat to sustain the momentum of "Catch the Rain", communities across the country have intensified efforts under the Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari: Catch the Rain (JSJB:CTR) campaign. Vizianagaram district of Andhra Pradesh has emerged as a compelling example of how Jan Bhagidari, coupled with scientific water management and convergence of government programmes, can significantly enhance groundwater recharge and strengthen long-term water security.

Under the Jaladhara Jalaharathi programme, implemented through convergence, the district undertook the restoration of traditional minor irrigation tanks and their feeder channels not merely to improve surface storage, but to revive natural recharge systems that replenish groundwater aquifers.

The district completed 8,973 water conservation works, including the rejuvenation of 6,424 Minor Irrigation tanks and 2,549 feeder channels, generating 1.28 crore person-days of employment while creating durable groundwater recharge assets.

Large-scale desilting and restoration removed nearly 109.9 lakh cubic metres of silt, cleared 82.48 lakh square metres of vegetation, and restored more than 2,090 kilometres of feeder channels, allowing rainwater to flow freely into tanks and recharge zones instead of being lost as runoff.

The interventions are expected to substantially improve groundwater availability across the district. The rejuvenated tank system is projected to create an additional storage potential of 0.70 TMC, while the restored feeder channels and tanks together are expected to contribute nearly 0.60 TMC of groundwater recharge, enhancing aquifer replenishment and improving the resilience of local water resources against recurring dry spells.

Recognising the importance of targeted groundwater management, the district prioritised 193 groundwater-deficit villages, where restoration works covered 596 feeder channels and 1,767 Minor Irrigation tanks. In addition, 94 cascade tank systems were rejuvenated to restore the natural hydrological connectivity between water bodies, improving infiltration and groundwater recharge across entire catchments.

The success of Vizianagaram demonstrates that sustainable groundwater management extends beyond engineering interventions, it depends on active public participation. Farmers, Gram Panchayats, local communities, frontline workers and district administration collectively revived traditional water bodies that had gradually lost their recharge capacity over time. Their participation reflects the spirit of Jan Bhagidari, transforming water conservation into a community-led movement.

As India continues the Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari: Catch the Rain campaign, Vizianagaram stands as an inspiring model of how reviving traditional water bodies can replenish groundwater, improve climate resilience and secure water resources for future generations.

Echoing the Prime Minister's call to "Catch the Rain, where it falls, when it falls," the district has demonstrated that every restored tank, every rejuvenated feeder channel and every participating citizen contributes to building a water-secure India.

item.content:encoded:
PIB Backgrounder
India as a Tourism Hub
Building a Globally Competitive, Inclusive and Sustainable Visitor Economy
Posted On: 31 JUL 2026 5:51PM by PIB Delhi

India is steadily emerging as a major tourism hub, backed by its civilisational heritage, natural diversity, spiritual appeal and expanding visitor economy. With stronger destination infrastructure, improved connectivity, digital platforms, travel facilitation and global promotion, the sector is moving towards higher-value tourism experiences. The focus is also on sustainable and inclusive growth, ensuring tourism supports local livelihoods, community participation, heritage preservation and India’s long-term competitiveness as a global destination.

Tourism as a National Growth Engine

Tourism has emerged as one of India's key drivers of economic growth, employment and regional development. More than a travel industry, it supports a wide ecosystem of hospitality, transport, handicrafts, food services, wellness, culture and local enterprises, creating livelihood opportunities across both urban and rural India. As domestic travel reaches record levels and international arrivals strongly continue to recover, the sector is playing an increasingly important role in strengthening local economies while showcasing India's rich cultural and natural heritage to the world.

Today, the sector reflects both scale and momentum:

  • 2.9 billion domestic tourist visits in 2024, exceeding pre-pandemic levels.
  • Around 2.02 crore International Tourist Arrivals 2025.
  • ₹15.73 lakh crore contribution to India's GDP in FY 2023-24, accounting for 5.22% of the economy.

  • 84.6 million jobs supported by tourism and hospitality in 2023-24.
  • Nearly USD 31.7 billion in international tourism receipts in 2025.

Yet, India's tourism story is not merely about rising visitor numbers. The country's unparalleled cultural heritage, diverse landscapes, spirituality, wellness traditions and experiential offerings provide a strong foundation to emerge as a leading global tourism destination.

India’s Tourism Advantage: Diversity, Demand and Soft Power

India's greatest tourism strength lies in the sheer diversity of experiences it offers. Within one country, visitors can explore ancient civilisations, living cultural traditions, sacred pilgrimage sites, pristine forests with diverse wildlife, snow-clad mountains, vibrant festivals, diverse cuisines and world-renowned wellness practices. This unique combination of tangible and intangible heritage enables our country to cater to a wide range of travellers throughout the year.

India's tourism asset base includes:

  • 44 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, reflecting the country's rich cultural and natural heritage.
  • 106 National Parks and 18 Biosphere Reserves, supporting wildlife and nature-based tourism.
  • A vast network of pilgrimage centres, heritage monuments, museums, protected forests, beaches, islands and cultural landscapes.
  • Rich traditions of handicrafts, cuisine, festivals, performing arts, Yoga and Ayurveda that continue to attract visitors from across the world.

Major Tourism Segments

India's tourism offerings span multiple high-potential segments, allowing destinations to cater to varied visitor interests and create year-round tourism demand.

Spiritual and Pilgrimage Tourism

As the birthplace of Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism and Sikhism, India is home to some of the world's most significant pilgrimage destinations. From the sacred circuits of Char Dham, Kashi and Ayodhya to the holy sites of Bodh Gaya, Amritsar, Tirupati and Puri, spiritual tourism continues to attract millions of domestic and international visitors every year. Continued investments in connectivity, infrastructure and visitor amenities are further strengthening India's position as a global spiritual tourism destination.

Buddhist Circuits and Transnational Cultural Linkages

India's Buddhist heritage continues to attract pilgrims and scholars from across Asia and beyond. Destinations associated with the life of Lord Buddha, together with other shared civilisational and cultural linkages, strengthen our nation’s role as an important centre for religious and cultural tourism.

Heritage and Cultural Tourism

India's rich civilisational legacy is reflected in its forts, palaces, temples, archaeological sites, museums and historic cities. Complementing these tangible treasures are the country’s vibrant living traditions—classical dance, music, festivals, handicrafts and regional cuisines—which offer visitors immersive cultural experiences beyond monuments. Together, they showcase the remarkable continuity and enduring vitality of India's cultural heritage across generations.

Virupaksha Temple, Hampi, Karnataka

Wellness, Yoga and Medical Tourism

India has emerged as a leading destination for wellness tourism, drawing visitors from around the world seeking holistic health and well-being. Yoga, recognised globally as India's gift to the world, along with Ayurveda, naturopathy and traditional healing systems, forms the foundation of this rapidly growing segment. Complementing these offerings are world-class healthcare facilities and high-quality, cost-effective medical treatment, which have further strengthened India's position as a preferred destination for medical tourism.

Eco-tourism and Wildlife Tourism

India's diverse ecosystems provide a wealth of nature-based tourism experiences. National parks, tiger reserves, wetlands, mangroves, biosphere reserves and Himalayan landscapes offer opportunities for wildlife safaris, birdwatching, trekking, turtle conservation trails, nature interpretation etc. At the same time, responsible eco-tourism is also creating sustainable livelihood opportunities for local communities while promoting conservation and protection of natural habitats.

Double Decker Living Root Bridge, Cherrapunjee, Meghalaya

Rural, Homestay and Community-based Tourism

Homestay in Himachal Pradesh


Beyond established destinations, rural tourism is bringing visitors closer to India's villages, local traditions and indigenous knowledge systems. Homestays, village walks, traditional cuisine, handicrafts, agricultural experiences and meaningful cultural interactions enable travellers to experience authentic local life while generating sustainable livelihoods and direct income for rural households, artisans and community enterprises.

 

MICE Tourism

India is emerging as a leading destination for Meetings, Incentives, Conferences and Exhibitions (MICE) tourism, supported by expanding convention infrastructure and a proven track record of hosting major international events. Modern convention centres, enhanced connectivity and destination-based business events are diversifying the country's tourism offerings beyond leisure travel, while generating year-round economic activity.

Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi

G20: Showcasing India's Tourism Potential to the World

India's G20 Presidency provided an unprecedented opportunity to showcase the country's tourism diversity on the global stage.

  • Over 200 G20 meetings were organised across more than 60 cities, taking international delegates beyond conventional metropolitan destinations.
  • The events highlighted India's heritage monuments, local crafts, regional cuisines, cultural performances and tourism experiences across different States and Union Territories.
  • The multi-city approach strengthened destination branding, promoted lesser-known locations and demonstrated India's capability to host world-class international events.
  • The experience has also reinforced India's growing potential as a destination for MICE tourism while enhancing its global visibility and soft power.

Coastal, Cruise, Adventure and Experiential Tourism

With a coastline spanning  over 7,500 km, island territories, rivers, vast deserts and mountain landscapes, India offers a diverse range of tourism experiences. From coastal and cruise tourism, to water sports, trekking, mountaineering, river rafting, desert safaris, film tourism and other experiential travel offerings- the country caters to a wide range of traveller interests. These diverse interests are expanding visitor choices and encouraging longer stays across destinations.

Infrastructure-Led Destination Development

India's tourism development strategy has progressively shifted from improving individual attractions to creating integrated destination ecosystems. The focus has shifted beyond developing standalone monuments and heritage sites to building holistic tourism destinations with seamless connectivity, high-quality visitor infrastructure and immersive experiences. This approach seeks to improve the overall visitor journey while ensuring that tourism generates sustained economic and long-term benefits for local communities.

Strengthening Destination Infrastructure

A number of flagship initiatives are driving this transformation across the country. These investments are shifting India's tourism model from isolated attractions to integrated destinations that encourage longer visitor stays, higher local spending and improved visitor experiences.

  • Swadesh Darshan has sanctioned 76 projects with an investment of over ₹5,295.24 crore across 14 thematic tourist circuits. Of these, 75 projects have been physically completed. The programme has developed infrastructure across the Buddhist, Coastal, Desert, Eco, Himalayan, North East, Ramayana, Rural, Spiritual, Tribal and other thematic circuits.
  • Building on this, Swadesh Darshan 2.0 adopts a destination-centric approach, focusing on sustainable and experience-based tourism. 53 projects, worth ₹2,207.08 crore, have been sanctioned to develop destinations through better planning, infrastructure and visitor experience.
  • Under the PRASHAD scheme, 54 projects worth over ₹1,726.24 crore have been sanctioned to improve infrastructure at major pilgrimage and heritage destinations, enhancing facilities for pilgrims while preserving their cultural and spiritual significance.
  • Through the Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment (SASCI), 40 projects across 23 States have been approved with an outlay of ₹3,295.76 crore for the development of iconic tourist centres and transform them to match global standards.
  • The Challenge-Based Destination Development (CBDD) initiative has sanctioned 37 projects worth ₹687.99 crore, focusing on destinations with high tourism potential under the spiritual and eco-tourism categories.

Connectivity as Tourism Infrastructure

Tourism infrastructure extends far beyond the destination itself. Improved accessibility has become a critical component of destination development.

Expansion of the national highway network, modernisation of railway stations, introduction of Vande Bharat trains, enhanced regional air connectivity through UDAN, airport development, better last-mile connectivity, e-buses and improved public amenities are making tourist destinations more accessible and reducing travel time. The next phase of regional connectivity, Viksit UDAN, with an outlay of over ₹28,840 crore, is expected to further strengthen air travel in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities and remote regions, including through the development of over 100 new aerodromes and 200 helipads. These investments are helping connect tourism circuits rather than keeping them as isolated attractions, enabling visitors to explore multiple destinations within a region.

Ease of Travel, Digital Tourism and Global Market Access

In an increasingly competitive tourism landscape, destinations are judged not only by what they offer but also by how easy they are to access, discover and experience. From visa facilitation and digital services to destination promotion and technology-driven innovation, India is steadily working to create a seamless visitor journey while strengthening its presence in global tourism markets.

Making Travel Easier

Travel facilitation has emerged as a key driver of international tourism. India has steadily simplified entry procedures through the e-Tourist Visa system, making travel more convenient for international visitors.

Key initiatives include:

  • e-Tourist Visa facility extended to nationals of 175 countries.
  • Entry permitted through 33 designated airports, 19 seaports and 4 land ports.
  • Expansion of visa categories and designated ports of entry under the e-Visa framework.
  • Continued efforts towards simplified documentation, digital authorisation and easier travel procedures for visitors from high-potential source markets.

Building a Digital Tourism Ecosystem

Digital platforms are becoming central to both visitor experience and tourism governance.

The National Integrated Database of Hospitality Industry (NIDHI+) has been developed as a unified digital platform for registration, recognition and classification of tourism service providers. It provides end-to-end online processing, integrated payment facilities and transparent approvals while improving ease of doing business.

Innovation Driving Tourism Growth

Innovation and entrepreneurship are emerging as important drivers of tourism growth. The travel and tourism sector has 1,497 DPIIT-recognised startups (as on 17 April 2023) across 262 districts, generating employment for nearly 13,919 people. Notably, 58% of these startups are based in Tier II and Tier III cities, highlighting the growing spread of tourism entrepreneurship beyond major urban centres.

These startups are developing solutions across travel-tech, online booking, homestays, rural and experiential tourism, smart mobility and AI-enabled travel planning. Notable examples include Highway Delite, which has created a digitally connected highway amenities network; VilloTale, which promotes rural tourism through homestays and community-based experiences; and udChalo, which provides technology-enabled travel services to over 2.8 million defence personnel, veterans and their dependants through digital platforms and a network of more than 70 booking offices.

Sustainable and Inclusive Tourism: The Long-Term Model

As India strengthens its position as a global tourism hub, sustainability is emerging as a key principle of tourism development. The focus is increasingly on creating destinations that are environmentally responsible, economically inclusive and capable of delivering high-quality visitor experiences. Alongside investments in infrastructure, connectivity and digital transformation, tourism policies are placing greater emphasis on responsible travel, community participation, skill development and long-term destination management.

Sustainable Destinations

India is promoting a more balanced model of tourism by encouraging Travel for LiFE and responsible visitor behaviour. Greater emphasis is also being placed on diversification through trekking, birdwatching, turtle trails and other nature-based experiences, helping distribute visitor flows beyond saturated destinations while also supporting conservation and local livelihoods. Sustainable tourism also contributes directly to the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by promoting inclusive economic growth, employment, cultural preservation and environmental protection.

  • SDG 8.9 focuses on promoting sustainable tourism that creates jobs and promotes local culture and products,
  • SDG 12.B emphasises on developing tools to monitor sustainable tourism impacts, and
  • SDG 14.7 highlights increasing the economic benefits to Small Island Developing States and Least Developed Countries through the sustainable use of marine resources, including tourism.

Looking Ahead

India's tourism vision extends beyond increasing visitor arrivals to building a resilient, high-value tourism ecosystem. Investments in destination infrastructure, enhanced connectivity, digital transformation, travel facilitation, skill development and sustainable destination management are strengthening India's competitiveness as a global tourism destination while ensuring that growth remains inclusive. By balancing economic development with environmental responsibility and community participation, the Government is creating a tourism sector that drives higher visitor spending, generates quality employment and delivers long-term economic and social benefits for destinations and local communities.

item.title: Strengthening India's Onion Value Chain: How VCF-SC Enabled Khemanand Dudh and Krishi Producer Company Ltd. to Empower Thousands of Farmers

item.description: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Strengthening India's Onion Value Chain: How VCF-SC Enabled Khemanand Dudh and Krishi Producer Company Ltd. to Empower Thousands of Farmers Posted On: 31 JUL 2026 5:44PM by PIB Delhi Mr. Prashant Sadashiv Lokhande, Promoter Access to modern post-harvest infrastructure and efficient market linkages has become essential for enhancing farmers' income and reducing post-harvest losses. item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Strengthening India's Onion Value Chain: How VCF-SC Enabled Khemanand Dudh and Krishi Producer Company Ltd. to Empower Thousands of Farmers
Posted On: 31 JUL 2026 5:44PM by PIB Delhi

Mr. Prashant Sadashiv Lokhande, Promoter

Access to modern post-harvest infrastructure and efficient market linkages has become essential for enhancing farmers' income and reducing post-harvest losses. One such inspiring example is Khemanand Dudh and Krishi Producer Company Limited, an Ahilyanagar-based enterprise that has transformed the onion value chain through an integrated post-harvest processing and procurement network. The company's journey demonstrates the transformative impact of the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes (VCF-SC) under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

The company established an integrated value chain development project for onion under the PMKSY–Operation Greens Scheme across five locations in Maharashtra. The project includes procurement, grading, sorting, packaging, cold storage and a dehydration plant, while also receiving support from the Ministry of Food Processing Industries, Government of India. Recognising the project's potential to strengthen agricultural infrastructure and improve farmers' livelihoods, the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castates extended financial assistance of ₹12 crore in 2023 through venture capital assistance comprising equity and optionally convertible debentures. The assistance enabled the company to strengthen its post-harvest processing infrastructure, expand procurement capacity and build an efficient supply chain connecting farmers with organised markets.

Post-Harvest Processing & Agricultural facility

The impact of the intervention has been significant. Today, the enterprise has expanded its farmer network to nearly 8,000 farmers, generated direct and indirect employment, created productive rural assets, achieved an annual revenue of ₹25.51 crore, and strengthened its net worth to ₹30 crore. The project has improved grading, handling and storage facilities, reduced post-harvest losses, enhanced price realisation for farmers, and established strong market linkages with institutional buyers and organised retail companies, thereby creating sustainable rural livelihoods.
Reflecting on the journey, Mr. Prashant Sadashiv Lokhande said:

"The support extended through the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes (VCF-SC), Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, strengthened our mission of empowering farmers through better market access and value addition. Today, Khemanand Dudh and Krishi Producer Company is helping farmers secure improved price realization, reduce wastage, and create sustainable rural livelihoods while contributing to inclusive agricultural growth."

Post-Harvest Processing & Agricultural Procurement Facility

The success of Khemanand Dudh and Krishi Producer Company Limited demonstrates how targeted financial assistance under the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes (VCF-SC) is enabling enterprises to build modern agricultural infrastructure, generate employment, improve farmers' incomes and strengthen rural economies. By promoting entrepreneurship and inclusive value-chain development, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to create sustainable livelihood opportunities and drive equitable economic growth across the country.

****

The life-saving organ was…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Railways
Indian Railways Successfully Transports India's First Live Donor Heart by Train; Vande Bharat Express Enables Life-saving Mission from Surat to Ahmedabad
Exemplary Coordination Between Indian Railways, RPF, Gujarat Police and Medical Teams Demonstrates Railways' Expanding Role in Life-saving Healthcare Services
Posted On: 31 JUL 2026 5:20PM by PIB Delhi

Indian Railways has achieved a historic milestone in the field of healthcare by successfully transporting a live donor heart by train for the first time in India. The life-saving organ was transported from Surat to Ahmedabad aboard Train No. 20901 Mumbai Central-Gandhinagar Capital Vande Bharat Express, ensuring its safe and timely arrival for transplantation at the U.N. Mehta Institute of Cardiology & Research Centre, Ahmedabad.

The landmark mission showcased the speed, punctuality and reliability of Vande Bharat Express while highlighting the growing role of Indian Railways in supporting critical healthcare services and emergency medical transportation.

Given the highly time-sensitive nature of organ transplantation, the operation required meticulous planning and seamless coordination among Indian Railways, the Railway Protection Force (RPF), Gujarat State Police and medical teams. Every stage of the transportation was carefully synchronised to ensure that the donor heart reached the recipient hospital within the prescribed viability window.

A dedicated Green Corridor was created from Platform No. 1 of Ahmedabad Railway Station to the U.N. Mehta Institute of Cardiology & Research Centre by the Railway Protection Force and Gujarat State Police, enabling uninterrupted movement of the donor heart and ensuring that the transplant procedure could commence without delay.

Speaking on the occasion, Shri Ved Prakash, Divisional Railway Manager, Ahmedabad, said,"This is a moment of immense pride and satisfaction for Indian Railways. The successful transportation of a live donor heart from Surat to Ahmedabad through Vande Bharat Express demonstrates our commitment to serving society beyond conventional passenger and freight transportation. In such life-saving missions, every minute is crucial. The excellent coordination among Indian Railways, RPF, Gujarat State Police and the medical teams ensured the success of this mission. Contributing towards saving a human life is not only our responsibility but also our highest duty towards service and humanity."

The successful mission further reinforces the capability of Vande Bharat Express to support time-critical operations through its high-speed connectivity, operational reliability and punctuality. It also demonstrates how modern railway infrastructure can play a crucial role in strengthening the country's emergency healthcare ecosystem.

Indian Railways expressed its appreciation to all stakeholders, including the Railway Protection Force, Gujarat State Police, doctors, organ transplant coordinators and railway officials, whose coordinated efforts made this challenging mission a success.

This historic achievement reaffirms Indian Railways' commitment to providing safe, reliable and efficient transportation services while extending its support to life-saving humanitarian initiatives and contributing to the nation's healthcare system.

*****

Mahesh Kumar/ Dr. Nayan Solanki/ Ritu Raj/ Manik Sharma

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Rural Development
EXPANSION OF SARAS AAJEEVIKA AND MARKET ACCESS FOR RURAL WOMEN SHGS
Posted On: 31 JUL 2026 5:20PM by PIB Delhi

Under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana–National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM), the Ministry of Rural Development is strengthening market access for Self Help Groups (SHGs) products through retail stores, organisation of SARAS Melas and promotion of SHG products through the digital marketing platform across the country, including Rajasthan. As per the Ministry’s guidelines all State Rural Livelihoods Missions (SRLMs), including Rajasthan, may organize at least two SARAS Fairs annually in their respective States. The Rajasthan State Rural Livelihoods Mission (Rajeevika) has identified locations for organizing SARAS Melas and establishing retail outlets under the State SHG brand, based on market potential and local requirements, to enhance market access for SHG products.

Under DAY-NRLM, the Ministry of Rural Development supports women SHGs, including those from small towns, rural and aspirational districts of Rajasthan, through a range of marketing interventions. These include development of State level SHG brands, training on packaging, labelling and product standardization, participation in SARAS Melas, exhibitions and trade fairs. The SHGs are also onboarded on eSARAS and on other e-commerce platforms. The capacity building initiative focuses on digital marketing and facilitation of participation in selected business fairs and exhibitions to promote export ready SHG products. The National Institute of Rural Development and Panchayati Raj regularly conducts capacity building and skill development programmes to support SHG members on product development, branding, packaging, quality improvement, digital marketing, enterprise management, export procedures and documentation, and market readiness to strengthen their access to domestic and international markets.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Rural Development DR. CHANDRA SEKHAR PEMMASANI in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Rural Development
FUNDS UNDER VB-G RAM G
Posted On: 31 JUL 2026 5:19PM by PIB Delhi

The Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) Act, 2025 has come into force with effect from 1st July, 2026 in rural areas of the entire country. All States and UTs have notified the VB G RAM G Scheme and have started implementing the same. The State/UT-wise details of interim allocation made, mother sanctions issued under the VB-G RAM G Scheme since its commencement on 01.07.2026 are given at Annexure.

There are no dues pertaining to any of the States/UTs are pending under Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) Scheme as on date.

The Government continuously monitors the implementation of the VB-G RAM G Scheme through the Management Information System (MIS), regular review meetings and other appropriate mechanisms. Prompt sanction of interim allocation and issuance of mother sanction has enabled the States/UTs to facilitate timely payment of wages under VB G RAM G.

The VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 provides a statutory framework for timely and effective implementation of the Scheme. The budgetary allocation of ₹ 95,692.31 made for the VB-G RAM G Scheme, for FY-2026-27 (for the period from 01.07.2026 to 31.03.2027) is among the largest ever allocation made at the Budget Estimate Stage for any rural employment scheme in the history of the country. Further a normative allocation of ₹ 95,692.31 crore has already been done among States/UTs and mother sanctions amounting to ₹ 25,844.97, as first installment, have also been issued. This will help in providing statutory guarantee of one hundred and twenty-five days of wage employment to every household whose adult members volunteer to undertake unskilled manual work. States/UTs have also been requested to expeditiously utilize the sanctioned fund and ensure timely payment of wages to the workers.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Rural Development
PROGRESS OF PRADHAN MANTRI AWAS YOJANA-GRAMIN (PMAY-G)
Posted On: 31 JUL 2026 5:17PM by PIB Delhi

A total of 33.54 lakh houses have been sanctioned and 35.54 lakh houses (inclusive of sanctions issued in previous years) have been completed under PMAY-G for the year 2025-26 upto June 2026. In the State of Jharkhand, 1.48 lakh houses have been sanctioned and 0.68 lakh houses have been completed under PMAY-G during this period.

As on date, a cumulative target of 4.18 crore houses have been allocated under the PMAY-G to the States and Union Territories (UTs) against which 3.92 crore houses have been sanctioned, 3.11 crore houses completed and 1.06 crore houses are remaining to be completed against allocated targets. State-wise/Union Territory-wise details of balance completion against targets, including State of Jharkhand are provided in Annexure I.

The State Governments/UT Administrations are the primary implementing authorities at the ground level. As reported by the States/UTs, the major reasons for delays in completion include cases of unwillingness of beneficiaries, permanent migration, disputed succession of deceased beneficiaries, delay in allotment of land to landless beneficiaries by the States/UTs, the delay in updation of credit confirmation from State IFMIS and at times General/Assembly/ Panchayat elections and unavailability of building materials.

The Ministry regularly reviews the progress reported by the States/UTs and takes up such implementation issues with them for timely resolution.

Under PMAY-G, the beneficiaries are provided financial assistance of ₹1.20 lakh in plain areas and ₹1.30 lakh in the North-Eastern Region States and 2 Hill States (Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand) and Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh. In addition to the Unit Assistance provided under the scheme, financial assistance of ₹12,000 is extended for the construction of toilets through convergence with the Swachh Bharat Mission-Gramin (SBM-G). Further, there is a provision for providing prescribed person-days of unskilled wage employment within the approved scheme parameters, at prevailing wage rates to each PMAY-G beneficiary for the construction of their house through convergence with MGNREGS/ VB G-RAM G.

PMAY-G households are also provided with piped drinking water through convergence with the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) and Har Ghar Nal Se Jal (HGNSJ) of the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, Ministry of Jal Shakti, or other similar schemes. In addition, beneficiaries are supported with electricity connection through relevant schemes implemented by the Ministry of Power, State Governments, or UT Administrations, and are provided Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) connections under the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas or other relevant schemes. Convergence under PMAY-G also includes the inclusion of women members of beneficiary households in Self-Help Groups (SHGs), thereby promoting their social and economic empowerment.

At the national level, as on date, a total of 3.10 crore houses have been provided with toilets, 2.45 crore houses with water connections, 3.08 crore houses with electricity connections, 2.91 crore houses with LPG connections, and 1.35 crore beneficiary households have been associated with Self-Help Groups (SHGs).

The approved duration of phase-2 of PMAY-G for completing additional 2 crore houses is March 2029. In this regard to complete the pending 1.06 crore houses, number of steps have been taken by the Government to accelerate construction of houses in all States/UTs including Jharkhand, to achieve the targets under PMAY-G. These include timely allocation of targets and release of adequate funds to the States/UTs, Regular review of progress, Monitoring and supervision of the scheme on a Dashboard, Regular Workshops by the Ministry with the States/UTs, Rural Mason Training program, etc.

The State wise, District-wise and Parliamentary Constituency wise details of rural road projects and the stages of construction under various verticals of PMGSY may be accessed at the programme website https://pmgsy.dord.gov.in/dbweb.

Under the road connectivity component of Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN), a total of 8000 km of road length, including bridges, is targeted to be constructed for providing all-weather connectivity to the unconnected Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups inhabited habitations across the country. The timeline for completion of PM-JANMAN is March 2028. Since inception, under PM-JANMAN,an amount of Rs. 1218 crore has been released against allocation of Rs. 4708 crore and the expenditure as on 26.07.2026 is Rs. 1542 crore.

Vibrant Villages Programme–I (VVP-I) is a Centrally Sponsored initiative of the Government of India aimed at improving infrastructure and quality of life in strategically important villages along the northern international border. Under VVP-I, 113 roads covering 1,085 Km and 35 bridges have been sanctioned to connect 137 habitations. As on 26.7.2026, 10 roads covering 248 Km have been completed and an amount of Rs.996.72 crores have been released. The State wise details of the projects sanctioned, completed and balance under VVP-I are given at Annexure-I. VVP-II is being implemented in convergence with PMGSY IV.

The Ministry had issued new technology initiatives guidelines in 2013 in order to use locally, marginally available materials/non-conventional materials/new materials in road construction. In order to encourage new materials in road construction, States/UTs were required to adopt new technologies in 15% of total proposals (10% using IRC mainstreaming technologies and 5% IRC accredited technologies). In order to promote and disseminate large scale adoption of New/Green Technologies in rural roads in a more systematic manner, the Ministry has revised these guidelines and brought out “Vision Document on New Technology Initiatives & Guidelines-2022” which requires the State Governments to propose minimum 50% of total length of annual proposals under New/ Green Technologies such as cement stabilization, lime stabilization, cold mix, waste plastics, cell-filled concrete, paneled cement-concrete pavement and fly ash.

Two interventions, namely, PMGSY-II for up-gradation of 50,000 km of the existing rural roads and PMGSY-III for consolidation of 1, 25,000 km Through Routes and Major Rural Links connecting habitations, inter-alia, to Gramin Agricultural Markets (GrAMs), Higher Secondary Schools and Hospitals, were added under the ambit of PMGSY to integrate the PMGSY roads to government facilities and institutions. Under PMGSY-III, a total of 6,96,620 facility centres have been connected with habitations, out of which 1,38,637 are agricultural markets, 1,46,784 are educational centres, 82,806 are medical centres and 3,28,393 are connected to transportation hubs.

As per the PMGSY guidelines, the contractors who constructed the road projects are required to provide maintenance during the five-year Defect Liability Period (DLP) for roads and bridges, post the construction. During the DLP, they are responsible for rectifying defects and maintain the road as per the prescribed standards. To ensure compliance with this maintenance obligation, the following measures have been implemented:

 (i) Mandatory contractual provision: The five-year maintenance obligation forms an integral part of the contract agreement executed with the contractor.

(ii) Performance-Based Maintenance Contract (PBMC): Maintenance during the Defect Liability Period is carried out through a Performance-Based Maintenance Contract, under which payments are linked to the prescribed service levels and road condition.

(iii) Regular inspections: Roads are inspected periodically by Programme Implementation Units (PIUs) and State Quality Monitors (SQMs) to assess compliance with prescribed maintenance standards and identify defects requiring rectification.

(iv) Digital monitoring through eMARG: The States/UTs have been advised to adopt the eMARG (Electronic Maintenance of Rural Roads) platform for digital monitoring of maintenance activities, recording inspections, reporting defects, tracking rectification, and processing maintenance payments.

(v) Quality monitoring mechanism: PMGSY follows a three-tier quality monitoring system comprising inspections by PIUs, State Quality Monitors (SQMs), and National Quality Monitors (NQMs) to ensure that roads are maintained in accordance with the prescribed standards.

(vi) Corrective action and contractual remedies: Contractors are required to rectify defects noticed during the DLP within the stipulated time. Failure to do so attracts action in accordance with the contract provisions, including withholding of maintenance payments, forfeiture of performance security, execution of repairs at the contractor's risk and cost, and other contractual remedies.

These measures are intended to ensure that rural roads constructed under PMGSY are adequately maintained during the mandatory five-year Defect Liability Period, thereby, preserving their quality, serviceability and longevity.

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Rural Development
item.description: Ministry of Rural Development EMPLOYMENT GUARANTEE AND LIVELIHOOD SUPPORT UNDER VB-G RAM G Posted On: 31 JUL 2026 5:15PM by PIB Delhi The Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) Act, 2025 has come into force with effect from 1st July, 2026 with the objective of enhancing livelihood security of rural households through a strengthened statutory framework for enhanced guaranteed wage employment of 125 days, creation of durable and productive rural assets, promotion of sustainable livelihoods and strengthening of rural infrastructure.…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Rural Development
EMPLOYMENT GUARANTEE AND LIVELIHOOD SUPPORT UNDER VB-G RAM G
Posted On: 31 JUL 2026 5:15PM by PIB Delhi

The Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) Act, 2025 has come into force with effect from 1st July, 2026 with the objective of enhancing livelihood security of rural households through a strengthened statutory framework for enhanced guaranteed wage employment of 125 days, creation of durable and productive rural assets, promotion of sustainable livelihoods and strengthening of rural infrastructure. The Act envisages a Whole-of-Government Approach by promoting convergence with other Central and State Government programmes and lays emphasis on Water-related Works, Core Rural Infrastructure, livelihood-related Infrastructure and works for the mitigation of extreme weather events, while encouraging technology-enabled planning, implementation, monitoring and transparency.

As per sub-section (2) of section 22 of the Act, the fund sharing pattern between the Central Government and the State Governments shall be 90:10 for the North Eastern States, Himalayan States and Union territory (Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir) and 60:40 for all other States and Union territories with legislature.

For the current financial year 2026–27, a Central share provision of ₹95,692.31 crore has been made for the Scheme, representing the largest allocation ever for rural employment at the Budget Estimate Stage. With the inclusion of the corresponding estimated State share, the total programme outlay is likely to exceed ₹1.51 lakh crore, which is expected to significantly accelerate rural transformation, large-scale employment generation and income enhancement in rural areas.

The VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 enhances the guaranteed employment from 100 days to 125 days in a financial year for every rural household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work. The Act further strengthens the statutory rights of workers by expressly providing for unemployment allowance where employment is not provided within the stipulated time and compensation for delay in payment of wages. It also provides for simplified mechanisms for registration and demand for employment. Further, wage payments under the Scheme are processed through the DBT-SPARSH platform, to facilitate timely, transparent and accountable transfer of wages directly into the bank accounts of workers. Further Gram Panchayat will continue to play important role in implementation of the scheme.

The VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 provides a comprehensive institutional framework for monitoring, evaluation and grievance redressal to ensure effective implementation of the Scheme and timely delivery of benefits to eligible rural households, including vulnerable workers. The implementation of the Scheme is monitored through a technology-enabled Management Information System (MIS), periodic review meetings at various levels, social audits, inspections and other monitoring mechanisms prescribed under the Act. The Act also provides for a time-bound, multi-tier grievance redressal mechanism at the Block and District levels for receiving and disposing of grievances relating to implementation of the Scheme. In addition, the Ministry provides technical support, capacity building and handholding to the States/UTs from time to time to strengthen its effective implementation. These measures are aimed at ensuring transparency, accountability, efficient service delivery and effective implementation of the VB-G RAM G Scheme in accordance with the provisions of the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Rural Development SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
NBA releases over ₹24 Lakh as Benefit Sharing to Farmers, Research Institutions and State Biodiversity Boards
Posted On: 31 JUL 2026 5:12PM by PIB Delhi

The National Biodiversity Authority has released over ₹24 lakh as Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) amount to benefit claimers, including buffalo farmers in Haryana, beneficiaries across 11 States, and three national research institutions. The amount has been released for conserving valuable biological resources that were later used by companies and research organisations for commercial utilisation. This demonstrates that farmers, breeders and institutes who conserve biological resources can receive fair and equitable benefit-sharing when their biological resources are used commercially.

The benefit-sharing amount has been disbursed among the identified beneficiaries including a family-run Murrah Buffalo Farm, Haryana (Rs. 4.30 lakh); ICAR–National Bureau of Plant Genetic Resources (NBPGR), New Delhi (Rs. 4.61 lakh); ICRISAT, Patancheru, Hyderabad (Rs. 5.36 lakh); ICAR–National Bureau of Fish Genetic Resources (NBFGR), Lucknow (Rs. 0.14 lakh); and the State Biodiversity Boards of Maharashtra (Rs. 3.22 lakh), Gujarat (Rs. 1.92 lakh), Telangana (Rs. 1.52 lakh), Karnataka (Rs. 0.73 lakh), Rajasthan (Rs. 0.63 lakh), Andhra Pradesh (Rs. 0.54 lakh), Madhya Pradesh (Rs. 0.46 lakh), Haryana (Rs. 0.44 lakh), Punjab (Rs. 0.19 lakh), Odisha (Rs. 0.17 lakh) and Tamil Nadu (Rs. 0.13 lakh).

The payment relates to access provided to Murrah buffalo breeding stock, one of India’s most commercial dairy buffalo breeds; hundreds of crop varieties, including rice, mustard, wild mung bean, chilli, tomato, cucumber, carrot, okra and other crops; 627 varieties of pearl millet; 55 maize varieties and fish cell cultures used in scientific research and cotton varieties. 

Under the National Biodiversity Authority’s ABS framework, benefit-sharing payments are disbursed in accordance with the approved regulations. The amounts allocated to research institutions will be utilized for biodiversity conservation and research activities. The ABS amount received from access to cotton genetic resources is distributed among the 11 cotton-growing States. In the case of individual conservers, such as farmers and breeders, the major share of the benefit-sharing amount is transferred through the concerned State Biodiversity Board for disbursement to the beneficiaries.

With this release, the NBA has disbursed a total of around ₹153 crore as Access and Benefit Sharing payments, reinforcing India’s commitment to  strengthen conservation, maintain biological collections, support scientific research, improve taxonomic studies, undertake biodiversity surveys and build capacity for biodiversity conservation. This would ensure that those who conserve the country’s biological resources receive a fair share of the benefits arising from their use.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Culture
National Digitization Drive Workshop Strengthens India’s Manuscript Preservation Framework; Union Minister of Culture Calls for Sustained National Effort in Digitization
Ministry of Culture organizes the National Digitization Drive Workshop in New Delhi under the Gyan Bharatam Mission
Posted On: 31 JUL 2026 4:46PM by PIB Delhi

India’s manuscript heritage spanning philosophy, Ayurveda, literature, mathematics, yoga, and diverse knowledge systems reflects the civilizational ethos of “jñānam paramam dhyeyam.” To advance this legacy, the Ministry of Culture convened the National Digitization Drive Workshop at The Ashok, New Delhi, under the Gyan Bharatam Mission, with participation from over 200 representatives of States/UTs, Centres, custodians, scholars, experts, and technology partners.

 

Appreciating the coordinated national effort, the Union Minister of Culture Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, said that, with the proactive support from all States, UTs, Ministry officials, Centres and custodians, over 1.2 crore manuscripts have been reported, marking a remarkable national milestone. The Union Minister added that the workshop is a coordinated national effort to safeguard centuries‑old knowledge, our saṅkalpa to respect the past, guide the present, and protect the future. Our Puravajas and Rishi‑munis created manuscripts across all disciplines, and it is our responsibility to categorize, codify, and publish them for future generations.

The Union Minister called for sustaining the national momentum and emphasized the need to maintain the current pace of work. He also said that digitization demands precision, discipline, and collaboration and stressed that preserving India’s knowledge systems with accuracy and integrity is a national responsibility.

Shri Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary Culture, stressed the need for a time‑bound, systematic, and coordinated work with all stakeholders to ensure uniformity, quality assurance, and seamless integration across the country. Shri Samar Nanda, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Culture welcomed all participants and reaffirmed the mission’s national goals, reminding everyone of the core framework of Gyan Bharatam and the collective responsibility to advance India’s manuscript preservation efforts.

 

Thereafter, Shri Inderjeet Singh, Director, Gyan Bharatam, Ministry of Culture presented an overview of the Gyan Bharatam Mission, outlining national objectives, digital infrastructure, and coordinated implementation. Further, Prof. Anirban Dash, Project Director, Gyan Bharatam, Ministry of Culture explained the mission’s two-phased functional pattern - technical and scholastic understanding to ensuring high‑quality digitization and rigorous knowledge validation.

The workshop, structured around five core themes, reviewed national digitization targets, standardized imaging and metadata practices, refined implementation strategies, showcased best performing States, addressed operational challenges, and developed a coordinated roadmap for a unified, standards driven national digitization framework. Presentations were made by Rajasthan, BORI Pune, Jammu & Kashmir, Asiatic Society Kolkata, a few Gyan Bharatam Centres - KOBA, Gujrat; Vrindavan Research Institute, Vrindavan; Sevadhi, Kerala; and Jamia Hamdard, Delhi; along with technology partners, highlighting field experiences, innovations, and scalable models.

 

The Ministry also showcased India’s emerging National Digital Manuscript Ecosystem, supported by AI platforms and a structured access policy framework. Recognizing the fragility of many manuscripts, the Ministry emphasized that conservation and digitization will proceed simultaneously, with States and Centres receiving funding to strengthen infrastructure, equipment, and trained manpower.

The workshop concluded with a shared commitment to accelerating national efforts. The National Digitization Drive marks a significant step toward building a unified, AI‑enabled manuscript ecosystem, ensuring that India’s civilizational knowledge is preserved, digitized, and made accessible for future generations.

item.content:encoded:
AYUSH
Union Ayush Minister Shri Prataprao Jadhav Recommends Arjuna Award for Mirabai Chanu
Shri Jadhav Writes to Union Sports Minister, recognising Chanu’s remarkable sporting achievements
Posted On: 31 JUL 2026 4:40PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Ayush and Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Shri Prataprao Ganpatrao Jadhav, has written to the Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports, Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, on his own initiative, urging that India's celebrated weightlifter and Olympic medallist, Mirabai Chanu, be considered for the prestigious Arjuna Award this year.

In his letter, Union Minister Shri Prataprao Jadhav highlighted Mirabai Chanu’s exceptional achievements and her remarkable contribution to Indian weightlifting. The Minister noted that the athlete from Manipur has created history through her outstanding performances at the Commonwealth Games, bringing immense pride to the nation.

Shri Prataprao Jadhav highlighted Chanu’s remarkable record of winning gold medals at successive editions of the Commonwealth Games and her distinction of being the athlete who won India’s first gold medal on each of these occasions. The Minister also highlighted her exceptional performances in the 48 kg category, including her record-breaking lifts in the snatch, clean and jerk and total lift categories.

Shri Jadhav further highlighted that Mirabai Chanu has already been honoured with several of the country’s highest sporting recognitions, including the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award and the Padma Shri, besides winning an Olympic medal. However, her childhood dream of receiving the Arjuna Award, which she had nurtured since her early days of training in her village in Manipur, remains unfulfilled.

Urging the Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports to consider her nomination, Shri Jadhav expressed that honouring Mirabai Chanu with the Arjuna Award would be a fitting recognition of her outstanding performances, exceptional talent and invaluable contribution to Indian sport.

Shri Prataprao Jadhav also emphasised that Chanu’s inspiring journey from a small village in Manipur to becoming one of India’s most accomplished weightlifters is a testament to her determination, perseverance and dedication, and serves as an inspiration to millions of young Indians.
